content.text:
I've submitted index 22 (Fe 0.58, Ni 0.26, V 0.16) as the best composition, at 9e-8 A photocurrent. With only three measurements, I can't tell whether it's the best in the library.

| Index | Composition (Fe / Ni / V) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | 0.58 / 0.26 / 0.16 | 9e-8 A |
| 81 | 0.55 / 0.31 / 0.14 | 9e-8 A (tie) |
| 126 | 0.43 / 0.20 / 0.37 | 1e-8 A |

- **How I chose where to measure:** I spent all 5 XRD scans first, spread across the composition space. Every scan shows the same substrate peaks (the conductive glass the films sit on); only the extra peaks change with composition.
  - The Fe-rich point shows peaks that look like an iron oxide, which could absorb light at the 2.06 eV illumination energy.
  - The Ni-rich point shows NiO. Its band gap is too wide (about 3.5 eV) to absorb that light.
  - The V-rich point shows a mix of vanadium-containing phases.
- **What the photocurrents suggest:** going from the Fe–V point (126) to the Fe-rich point (22) raised photocurrent about ninefold, so more V seems to hurt. I spent the last measurement on another Fe-rich, low-V point (81), which tied with 22. I kept 22 because it has the most Fe.
- **What's untested:** I never measured the Ni-rich or V-rich regions, and ruled them out only from XRD and the one trend above. The better Fe-rich candidates I didn't reach are 46 (Fe 0.58, V 0.20) and 144 (Fe 0.50, V 0.13).
